summary: A fungal leaf disease commonly associated with concentric brown lesions, often beginning on older leaves.
verify: Check whether the spots are dry, brown, and roughly circular, and whether older foliage is affected first.
care: Reduce prolonged leaf wetness, improve airflow, sanitize infected plant debris, and use locally approved crop-specific guidance for any control product.

summary: A serious oomycete disease that can produce rapidly enlarging dark lesions, especially under cool, humid conditions.
verify: Look for rapidly expanding dark lesions and a history of cool/wet weather. Compare with bacterial spot and early blight.
care: Remove severely affected material where appropriate, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and seek local extension guidance promptly because outbreaks can spread quickly.

summary: A bacterial disease that can cause small dark leaf spots and lesions on fruit or stems.
verify: Check whether spots are small and dark and whether similar symptoms occur on stems or fruit.
care: Avoid handling plants while foliage is wet, sanitize tools, and use locally recommended sanitation and management practices.

summary: A disease favored by high humidity that often produces yellow areas on the upper leaf surface with olive or grayish growth underneath.
verify: Inspect the underside of leaves, especially in dense canopies or humid conditions.
care: Increase ventilation, reduce humidity and leaf wetness, and remove affected debris according to local guidance.

summary: A leaf-spot disease that typically creates numerous small lesions, often with pale centers and darker margins.
verify: Look for many small spots concentrated on lower leaves and inspect whether centers contain tiny dark specks.
care: Limit splash and prolonged wetness, remove infected debris, and improve airflow where possible.

summary: A viral disease commonly associated with leaf curling, yellowing, stunting, and whitefly transmission.
verify: Check for curling/yellowing on young leaves and inspect plants for whiteflies. Compare with nutrient and herbicide injury.
care: Focus on clean planting material, weed management, vector management, and removal of infected plants according to local extension recommendations.

summary: A fungal disease of potato foliage that commonly causes dark spots, often with concentric rings, and can reduce leaf area.
verify: Check for target-like rings on older leaves and compare with late blight.
care: Maintain plant vigor, limit leaf wetness, remove volunteer plants/debris, and follow local crop-protection guidance.

summary: A fast-moving disease that can cause dark, water-soaked-looking lesions and rapid foliage collapse under favorable weather.
verify: Inspect for rapidly expanding lesions and check recent cool, wet weather.
care: Monitor frequently, reduce wetness where feasible, remove severely affected material appropriately, and seek local extension advice quickly.

summary: A fungal disease that produces olive-to-brown lesions on leaves and fruit and is favored by wet spring conditions.
verify: Look for olive or brown scabby spots on leaves or fruit and compare with insect damage.
care: Improve orchard sanitation, remove fallen leaves where practical, and use locally recommended disease-management schedules.

summary: A fungal leaf disease characterized by rust-colored pustules on leaf surfaces.
verify: Inspect both leaf surfaces for small rust-colored pustules and distinguish from other leaf-spot diseases.
care: Use resistant varieties where available and follow local disease-monitoring recommendations.
